questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.factOneLiner: Canberra was built as a compromise after Sydney and Melbourne both wanted the title.

questions.prompt: How many strings does a standard violin have?
questions.factOneLiner: The four strings are tuned in perfect fifths: G, D, A and E.

questions.prompt: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
questions.factOneLiner: The red comes from iron oxide, essentially rust, spread across its surface.

questions.prompt: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
questions.factOneLiner: It hung in Napoleon's bedroom for a few years before it moved to the Louvre.

questions.prompt: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.factOneLiner: It covers more area than every piece of dry land on the planet combined.

questions.prompt: Which French general crowned himself emperor in 1804?
questions.factOneLiner: He took the crown from the pope's hands and placed it on his own head.

questions.prompt: Which gas do plants absorb from the air to grow?
questions.factOneLiner: A large tree can pull tens of kilograms of it out of the air every year.

questions.prompt: What is the longest river in Africa?
questions.factOneLiner: It runs through eleven countries before it reaches the Mediterranean.

questions.prompt: In which country would you find the Great Barrier Reef?
questions.factOneLiner: It is made of roughly nine hundred islands and nearly three thousand separate reefs.

questions.prompt: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.factOneLiner: It is the only metal that stays liquid at ordinary room temperature.

questions.prompt: Who wrote the play Romeo and Juliet?
questions.factOneLiner: He wrote it early in his career, around 1595.

questions.prompt: How many sides does a hexagon have?
questions.factOneLiner: Honeybees build in hexagons because that shape wastes the least wax.

questions.prompt: Which country gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States?
questions.factOneLiner: It arrived in 1885 packed into more than two hundred crates.

questions.prompt: What is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.factOneLiner: It is nothing but carbon, arranged under enormous pressure.

questions.prompt: What is the tallest mountain above sea level?
questions.factOneLiner: Measured from its own base instead, Mauna Kea is actually taller.

questions.prompt: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.factOneLiner: It came down after a press conference announced the new rules early by mistake.

questions.prompt: What is the main ingredient in guacamole?
questions.factOneLiner: The name comes from the Aztec word ahuacatl.

questions.prompt: Which sea creature has three hearts?
questions.factOneLiner: Two pump blood to the gills and one pumps it to the rest of the body.

questions.prompt: Which language has the most native speakers in the world?
questions.factOneLiner: Around nine hundred million people speak it as a first language.

questions.prompt: Who was the first person to walk on the moon?
questions.factOneLiner: He and Buzz Aldrin spent about two and a half hours outside the module.
